item.title: Episode 15 - Portrait of a Rebirth: The Lili Elbe Story • The Dot Femme Podcast
item.description: In this episode, Dany and Claire travel to 1930s Paris and Dresden to uncover the story of Lili Elbe — the pioneering transgender woman whose courage and tragedy reshaped the early history of gender-affirming care and forever changed the way we understand identity.

item.title: Episode 16 - Brains Over Bullets: Alan Turing Part 1 • The Dot Femme Podcast
item.description: Dany and Claire travel to Bletchley Park to uncover how Alan Turing’s genius helped crack Nazi Germany’s Enigma code and invent the blueprint for modern computing—long before the world understood what he was building.

item.title: Episode 17 - The Enigma of Alan Turing (Part 2) • The Dot Femme Podcast
item.description: In the aftermath of World War II, Alan Turing pioneered artificial intelligence and modern biology—only to be persecuted for being gay. Dany and Claire explore his final years, his tragic death, and how his legacy endures as a symbol of queer brilliance and resilience.

item.title: Episode 18 - Making a Silent Massacre: The AIDS Crisis (Part 1) • The Dot Femme Podcast
item.description: On a stormy afternoon in 1982, Dany and Claire take an overarching look at the AIDS Crisis of Ronald Reagan's 1980s and the political environment that created a silent massacre in the first part of this four part miniseries for HIV Awareness Month.

item.title: Episode 19 – From Mystery to Breakthrough: The AIDS Crisis (Part 2)
item.description: In part two of this four-part miniseries, Dany and Claire take a look at the science and medical research that took HIV from a certain death sentence to a manageable disease.

item.title: Episode 20 - Organize to Survive: The AIDS Crisis (Part 3) • The Dot Femme Podcast
item.description: In the penultimate installment of our four-part HIV Awareness Month miniseries, Dany and Claire explore how queer communities became caregivers, researchers, pharmacists, smugglers, lawyers, activists, and even nuns to survive a global plague in an era of political apathy and moral condemnation.

item.title: Episode 21 - Time to ACT UP: The AIDS Crisis (Part 4) • The Dot Femme Podcast
item.description: In the final part of our deep dive into the AIDS crisis, Dany & Claire explore the life and legacy of New York activist Larry Kramer and ACT UP—the AIDS Coalition to Unleash Power—and how direct action transformed collective grief into lasting change.

item.title: Episode 22 - (Gender)F%&#ing Peasant Revolts • The Dot Femme Podcast
item.description: It’s festival season in Medieval Europe, and for the first episode of season 2, Dany and Claire take a moment to see how queerness and peasant revolts are inherently linked. Because history shows that when hierarchies get restrictive, gender gets weird.

item.title: Episode 23 - 404: Straight Not Found • The Dot Femme Podcast
item.description: It's the 90's, baby! And the queer community is evolving thanks to a little thing called "The Internet." Join Dany and Claire in a corner internet cafe as they learn all about the (queer) history of the internet and why the modern queer community wouldn't exist without it.

item.title: Episode 24 - The Panic Playbook: Fear, blackmail, and the Lavender Scare • The Dot Femme Podcast
item.description: Dany and Claire spend some time in the Washington D.C. of the 1950s and take a long, hard look at the Cold War’s other social panic: The Lavender Scare.
